name: Bodega (SQLiteStorageEngine)
baseline: One file per object on disk (Bodega's DiskStorageEngine, the plain FileManager write pattern)
verdict_reason: The docs give about 0.1 s against 0.25 s to load 1,000 objects and say the gap grows with object count, which the charts show widening into the thousands. The result matches the known cost of per-file system calls, though it is the author's own comparison of two of his engines.
tier_reason: First-party figures stated as a rule of thumb, with charts but no device, OS or build configuration.
claimed_speedup: Loading 1,000 objects: about 0.1 seconds with SQLiteStorageEngine vs about 0.25 seconds with DiskStorageEngine (2.5x, derived from page data); larger counts appear only in charts.
workload: Reading (initializing from storage) and writing 1,000 to 10,000 small objects stored as Data blobs keyed by CacheKey.
one_liner: Key-value store whose SQLite engine loads 1,000 objects in about 0.1 s against 0.25 s for one-file-per-object storage.
how_it_is_fast: SQLiteStorageEngine keeps every object as a row in one SQLite database (through SQLite.swift), so a batch read or write is a few statements in one transaction. One-file-per-object storage pays an open, read or write, and close (plus directory updates) for every object, and that cost grows with the number of files.
use_it_when: Persisting thousands of small Codable objects or blobs (API responses, app state) with a simple key-value API
Replacing hand-rolled one-file-per-object caches whose launch time grows with object count
skip_it_when: Large blobs such as full-size images, where individual files avoid SQLite page overhead
You need to inspect or sync the stored files with ordinary file tools
caveats: A comparison between Bodega's own two engines, not against hand-written FileManager code
The text figures are an approximate 'rule of thumb'; per-count values are only in charts
No device, OS or build configuration given
tradeoffs: Stored data is opaque without an SQLite viewer

evidence.quote: a rule of thumb is that loading 1,000 objects from disk takes about 0.25 seconds
By comparison if you're using ``SQLiteStorageEngine`` it only takes about 0.1 seconds to load 1,000 objects, the difference only growing more the more objects you have.
